# CS 29.1305 — Powerplant instruments

> [!summary]
> CS 29.1305 lists the powerplant instruments a large rotorcraft must carry. It
> is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft applicant owns
> it. The list has three parts: twenty-seven items for every rotorcraft, four
> more for Category A and two for Category B. Nine items read a turbine engine
> parameter, so the engine applicant supplies the signal, the connection or the
> declared limit behind them. Three items depend on a rating the engine
> applicant elects to claim.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

The paragraph opens "The following are the required powerplant instruments:"
[ext CS 29.1305]. Most items are noun phrases, so their force comes from that
lead-in and not from a verb of their own.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Sub-points (a)(1) to (a)(27) apply to each rotorcraft. | Statement |
| **(a)(1)** | A carburettor air temperature indicator for each reciprocating engine. | Required |
| **(a)(2)** | A cylinder head temperature indicator for each air-cooled reciprocating engine, and a coolant temperature indicator for each liquid-cooled reciprocating engine. | Required |
| **(a)(3)** | A fuel quantity indicator for each fuel tank. | Required |
| **(a)(4)** | A low-fuel warning device for each fuel tank which feeds an engine. | Required |
| **(a)(4)(i)** | Provide a warning to the crew when approximately 10 minutes of usable fuel remains in the tank. | Required |
| **(a)(4)(ii)** | Be independent of the normal fuel quantity indicating system, or be designed and constructed so as to meet the minimum safety objectives compatible with the most severe hazard induced by the combination of any failures of the fuel quantity indicator device and the low-fuel level warning device. | Required |
| **(a)(5)** | A means to indicate the manifold pressure for each reciprocating engine of the altitude type. | Required |
| **(a)(6)** | An oil pressure indicator for each pressure-lubricated gearbox. | Required |
| **(a)(7)** | An oil pressure warning device for each pressure-lubricated gearbox, to indicate when the oil pressure falls below a safe value. | Required |
| **(a)(8)** | An oil quantity indicator for each oil tank and each rotor drive gearbox, if lubricant is self-contained. | Required |
| **(a)(9)** | An oil temperature indicator for each engine. | Required |
| **(a)(10)** | An oil temperature warning device to indicate unsafe oil temperatures in each main rotor drive gearbox, including gearboxes necessary for rotor phasing. | Required |
| **(a)(11)** | A means to indicate the gas temperature for each turbine engine. | Required |
| **(a)(12)** | A means to indicate the gas producer speed for each turbine engine. | Required |
| **(a)(13)** | A tachometer for each engine that, if combined with the applicable instrument required by sub-paragraph (a)(14), indicates rotor rpm during autorotation. | Required |
| **(a)(14)** | At least one tachometer to indicate, as applicable, the rotor speed of (a)(14)(i), (a)(14)(ii) and (a)(14)(iii). | Required |
| **(a)(14)(i)** | The rpm of the single main rotor. | Statement |
| **(a)(14)(ii)** | The common rpm of any main rotors whose speeds cannot vary appreciably with respect to each other. | Statement |
| **(a)(14)(iii)** | The rpm of each main rotor whose speed can vary appreciably with respect to that of another main rotor. | Statement |
| **(a)(15)** | A free power turbine tachometer for each turbine engine. | Required |
| **(a)(16)** | A means, for each turbine engine, to indicate power for that engine. | Required |
| **(a)(17)** | For each turbine engine, an indicator to indicate the functioning of the power plant ice protection system. | Required |
| **(a)(18)** | An indicator for the fuel filter required by CS 29.997, to indicate the occurrence of contamination of the filter to the degree established in compliance with CS 29.955. | Required |
| **(a)(19)** | For each turbine engine, a warning means for the oil strainer or filter required by CS 29.1019, if it has no bypass, to warn the pilot of the occurrence of contamination of the strainer or filter before it reaches the capacity established in accordance with CS 29.1019(a)(2). | Required |
| **(a)(20)** | An indicator to indicate the functioning of any selectable or controllable heater used to prevent ice clogging of fuel system components. | Required |
| **(a)(21)** | An individual fuel pressure indicator for each engine, unless the fuel system which supplies that engine employs no pumps, filters or other components subject to degradation or failure which may adversely affect fuel pressure at the engine. | Required |
| **(a)(22)** | A means to indicate to the flight crew the failure of any fuel pump installed to show compliance with CS 29.955. | Required |
| **(a)(23)** | Warning or caution devices to signal to the flight crew when ferromagnetic particles are detected by the chip detection system required by CS 29.1337(e). | Required |
| **(a)(24)** | For auxiliary power units, an individual indicator, warning or caution device, or other means to advise the flight crew that limits are being exceeded, if exceeding these limits can be hazardous, for the three parameters in (a)(24)(i), (a)(24)(ii) and (a)(24)(iii). | Required |
| **(a)(24)(i)** | Gas temperature. | Statement |
| **(a)(24)(ii)** | Oil pressure. | Statement |
| **(a)(24)(iii)** | Rotor speed. | Statement |
| **(a)(25)** | For rotorcraft for which a 30-second/2-minute OEI power rating is requested, provide a means to alert the pilot when the engine is at the 30-second and 2-minute OEI power levels, when the event begins, and when the time interval expires. | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(26)** | For each turbine engine utilising 30-second/2-minute OEI power, provide a device or system for use by ground personnel which meets (a)(26)(i) to (a)(26)(iv). | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(26)(i)** | Automatically records each usage and duration of power at the 30-second and 2-minute OEI levels. | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(26)(ii)** | Permits retrieval of the recorded data. | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(26)(iii)** | Can be reset only by ground maintenance personnel. | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(26)(iv)** | Has a means to verify proper operation of the system or device. | Required if claimed |
| **(a)(27)** | For rotorcraft for which a 30-minute power rating is claimed, provide a means to alert the pilot when the engines are at the 30-minute power rating levels, when the event begins, when the time interval expires and, if a cumulative limit in one flight exists, when the cumulative time in one flight is reached. | Required if claimed |
| **(b)** | Sub-points (b)(1) to (b)(4) apply to Category A rotorcraft, in addition to (a). | Statement |
| **(b)(1)** | An individual oil pressure indicator for each engine, and either an oil pressure warning for each engine or a master warning device for all engines with means for isolating the individual warning circuit from the master warning device. | Required |
| **(b)(2)** | An independent fuel pressure warning device for each engine, or a master warning device for all engines with provision for isolating the individual warning device from the master warning device. | Required |
| **(b)(3)** | Fire warning indicators. | Required |
| **(b)(4)** | When the OEI Training Mode is prescribed, provide a means to indicate to the pilot the simulation of an engine failure, the annunciation of that simulation, and a representation of the OEI power being provided. | Required |
| **(c)** | Sub-points (c)(1) and (c)(2) apply to Category B rotorcraft, in addition to (a). | Statement |
| **(c)(1)** | An individual oil pressure indicator for each engine. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Fire warning indicators, when fire detection is required. | Required |

Three rows carry Required if claimed rather than Required. Sub-points (a)(25)
and (a)(26) bind only where a 30-second/2-minute OEI power rating is requested,
and (a)(27) only where a 30-minute power rating is claimed
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(27)]. The rating is elective for the engine applicant; once
it is claimed, the instrument is mandatory for the rotorcraft.

The lettered rows (a), (b) and (c) are Statement. They set which rotorcraft the
list below them applies to and impose nothing of their own. Category A and
Category B are rotorcraft certification categories, not engine declarations, and
`engine_profile.md` carries no category.

Sub-point (b)(4) is written as Required, not Required if claimed. The condition
is that "the OEI Training Mode is prescribed" [ext CS 29.1305(b)(4)], which is a
property of the rotorcraft certification basis rather than something the
applicant elects in the way a rating is claimed. Where it is prescribed, the
means is mandatory.

Sub-points (a)(6), (a)(7), (a)(8) and (a)(10) concern gearbox lubrication, and
(a)(7) is the low oil pressure indication that starts the clock in the
loss-of-lubrication test of [[CS 29.927|CS 29.927(c)]]: that test begins upon
the indication to the flight crew that a lubrication failure has occurred.

### Where CS-27 differs

The two lists are not the same list with different labels. Six differences are
substantive for a turboshaft installation.

**Structure.** CS-29 divides its list in three: (a) for each rotorcraft, (b) for
Category A and (c) for Category B. CS-27 has one flat list, (a) to (w), that
applies to every small rotorcraft, and no category split in this paragraph.

**Turbine engine instruments.** This is the largest gap, and it runs in CS-29's
favour. The gas producer speed of (a)(12), the free power turbine tachometer of
(a)(15), the power indication of (a)(16) and the autorotation tachometer of
(a)(13) have no counterpart in CS-27. CS-27 asks only for the gas temperature
[ext CS 27.1305(n)] and, where a torque limitation is established in
CS 27.1521(e), a means for the pilot to determine torque [ext CS 27.1305(o)].
CS-29 has no torque item of its own; it asks for power instead.

**Piston engine wording.** CS-29 names the reciprocating engine in each piston
item, in (a)(1), (a)(2) and (a)(5), and adds a coolant temperature indicator for
each liquid-cooled reciprocating engine. CS-27 writes the same items without
naming the engine cycle, as a carburetor air temperature indicator for each
engine having a pre-heater [ext CS 27.1305(a)], a cylinder head temperature
indicator for each air cooled engine [ext CS 27.1305(b)], and manifold pressure
for each altitude engine [ext CS 27.1305(e)]. CS-27 has no coolant temperature
item.

**Gearbox oil instruments.** CS-29 requires an oil pressure indicator and an oil
pressure warning device for each pressure-lubricated gearbox, with no further
condition [ext CS 29.1305(a)(6)], [ext CS 29.1305(a)(7)]. CS-27 limits its two
gearbox oil warning devices to a main rotor drive gearbox "having an oil system
independent of the engine oil system" [ext CS 27.1305(g)]. CS-29 also requires
an oil quantity indicator for each rotor drive gearbox where the lubricant is
self-contained [ext CS 29.1305(a)(8)]; CS-27 requires one for each oil tank only
[ext CS 27.1305(i)].

**Fuel pressure.** CS-29 requires an individual fuel pressure indicator for each
engine, with a narrow relief where the fuel system supplying that engine has no
pumps, filters or other components subject to degradation or failure
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(21)]. CS-27 requires one for each pump-fed engine
[ext CS 27.1305(c)], which is a wider condition.

**Items CS-27 does not have at all.** The auxiliary power unit item of (a)(24),
the fire warning indicators of (b)(3) and (c)(2), the OEI Training Mode
indication of (b)(4), and the master warning arrangements of (b)(1) and (b)(2)
have no counterpart in CS-27.

The three rating-driven items exist in both codes with the same words and
different labels. The pilot alerting duty for the 30-second and 2-minute OEI
levels is (a)(25) here and (t) in CS-27; the ground recording device is (a)(26)
here and (u); the 30-minute power alerting duty is (a)(27) here and (w). A label
must never be carried across. The CS-27 text of that last item contains an
evident typographical slip, recorded in [[CS 27.1305]].

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.1305 creates no CS-E obligation. The instruments are fitted in the
rotorcraft, and the rotorcraft applicant provides them. The paragraph still
matters to the engine applicant, because most items on the list read an engine
parameter. Each one implies a connection, a signal or a declared limit that the
engine has to supply through the instructions for installation required by
[CS-E 20(d)] and the instrument list required by [CS-E 60(b)].

**The four turbine channels.** The gas temperature of (a)(11), the gas producer
speed of (a)(12), the free power turbine tachometer of (a)(15) and the power
indication of (a)(16) are all engine parameters, and (a)(13) adds an engine
tachometer that has to combine with the rotor tachometer during autorotation.
[[CS-E 60|CS-E 60(b)]] requires the engine applicant to list the instruments
necessary for control of the engine and to state the overall limits of accuracy
and transient response required of them. [[CS-E 40|CS-E 40(g)]] then requires
those limits to be taken into account in determining the engine performance and
operating limitations, and [[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(e)]] requires the performance data
from which the rotorcraft applicant derives a power indication.

[VERIFY: whether this engine has a free power turbine. Sub-point (a)(15)
requires a free power turbine tachometer for each turbine engine, and
`engine_profile.md` records the power turbine architecture as not declared. The
same open item already blocks several CS-E notes.]

**Oil instruments.** The oil temperature indicator of (a)(9), the oil quantity
indicator of (a)(8) for each oil tank, and the individual oil pressure indicator
of (b)(1) and (c)(1) read the engine oil system. [[CS-E 570]] supplies all
three: "Each oil tank must have, or have provision for, an oil quantity
indicator" [CS-E 570(f)(2)], and provision must be made near each oil pressure
connection provided for instrumentation, to limit the loss of fluid if a pipe
fails [CS-E 570(a)(4)]. Where the pressure is sensed is engine-side work as
well, and [[AMC E 60|AMC E 60(2)(a)]] governs it.

[VERIFY: whether "each pressure-lubricated gearbox" in (a)(6) and (a)(7) reaches
a gearbox inside the engine type design, or only the rotor drive gearboxes.
CS-29 does not qualify the phrase, where CS-27 limits its equivalent to a
gearbox with an oil system independent of the engine oil system. The answer
decides whether the engine supplies a further oil pressure connection.]

**Oil filter warning.** Sub-point (a)(19) asks for a warning means for the oil
strainer or filter, for each turbine engine, where the filter has no bypass.
[[CS-E 570]] carries the engine side of the same condition: if the most critical
main oil filter has no by-pass, it must have "provision for appropriate
indication to the flight crew of impending blockage" [CS-E 570(b)(2)], and where
a by-pass exists, indication of by-pass operation must be provided for
maintenance action [CS-E 570(c)(2)].

**Fuel instruments.** The individual fuel pressure indicator of (a)(21) and the
fuel pressure warning device of (b)(2) read the engine fuel inlet, and
[[CS-E 560]] requires provision near each fuel pressure connection provided for
instrumentation, to limit fluid loss if a pipe fails [CS-E 560(f)]. The engine's
own filter indication duty is separate from (a)(18): it is the impending
blockage indication of [CS-E 560(b)(2)], to the flight crew or to the
maintenance crew.

Sub-points (a)(18), (a)(19), (a)(22) and (a)(23) name CS 29.955, CS 29.997,
CS 29.1019 and CS 29.1337. Those are airframe points, and this vault does not
hold them in sliced form. The reference is recorded and not followed.

**Ice protection indication.** Sub-point (a)(17) asks for an indicator of the
functioning of the power plant ice protection system. On the engine side this is
the general provision duty of [CS-E 60(a)], and [[AMC E 60|AMC E 60(1)]] names
"indication of engine ice protection system activation" as an example of
instrumentation that may be required for aircraft certification. The engine
operating obligation in icing is [[CS-E 780]], which is a functioning
requirement and not an instrument requirement.

**Chip detection.** Sub-point (a)(23) requires the warning or caution devices;
the detection system itself is required elsewhere in CS-29 and is not sliced
here. CS-E imposes no chip detection instrument. It does assume the hardware:
[[AMC E 570|AMC E 570(4)]] states that, in complying with CS-E 570(a)(2),
"access points include, but are not limited to, Magnetic Chip Detectors and
gearbox access cover plates". The engine applicant therefore declares the
detector as an interface under [CS-E 20(d)], and the signalling is the
rotorcraft's.

**OEI alerting and recording.** Sub-points (a)(25) and (a)(26) run parallel to
[[CS-E 60|CS-E 60(d)]], which this engine triggers because `engine_profile.md`
declares 30-Second OEI and 2-Minute OEI Power. [[AMC E 60]] already sets out how
the two sides map onto each other, including the reset authority and the
maintenance alerting duty that CS-E adds. That account is not repeated here.

**30-minute power alerting.** `engine_profile.md` declares Rated 30-Minute Power
under [[CS-E 40|CS-E 40(b)(4)]], so sub-point (a)(27) applies to a CS-29
installation of this engine. No CS-E sub-point mirrors it: CS-E 60(d) reaches
only the 30-Second and 2-Minute OEI levels [CS-E 60(d)]. The engine-side duty is
therefore the general one — provision for the instrumentation necessary to
ensure operation within the engine operating limitations [CS-E 60(a)] — plus the
30-minute limitations themselves, and the cumulative limit in one flight if the
applicant sets one, delivered through [CS-E 20(d)].

**OEI Training Mode.** No CS-E Amendment 8 paragraph in scope names an OEI
Training Mode, so (b)(4) imposes nothing on the engine directly. The
representation of OEI power it displays still draws on the engine performance
data of [CS-E 20(e)] and on the OEI performance characteristics and variability
that [CS-E 20(f)] requires for power assurance procedures.

Several items reach no CS-E obligation at all. The carburettor air temperature
indicator of (a)(1), the cylinder head and coolant temperature indicators of
(a)(2) and the manifold pressure means of (a)(5) are reciprocating engine
instruments by their own wording, and a turboshaft produces none of those
parameters. The fuel tank instruments of (a)(3) and (a)(4) and the fuel system
heater indicator of (a)(20) belong to the aircraft fuel system. The gearbox
warning devices of (a)(7) and (a)(10) belong to the rotor drive system, whose
testing regime is [[CS 29.927]]. The fire warning indicators of (b)(3) and
(c)(2) are detection, which [[CS-E 130]] does not address: that paragraph is
fire prevention and containment on the engine. The auxiliary power unit item of
(a)(24) is outside the declared application, since `engine_profile.md` declares
a rotorcraft turboshaft in a multi-engine propulsion installation.

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-29 or CS-27, and,
under CS-29, whether it is Category A or Category B. The category decides
whether (b) or (c) adds to the list. [[CS-E 30]] carries the code question as an
open item.]
